why_this_works: Seeding the Romas removes excess water so you get a thick, chunky salsa instead of soup. The lime juice and hot sauce deliver both acid and heat, which brightens the raw tomatoes and balances the cilantro's sharpness. Blending to your preferred consistency means you control the texture — chunky or smooth.

steps: Seed and chop the Roma tomatoes.
Roughly chop the cilantro and green onions.
Combine tomatoes, jalapeños, cilantro, and green onions in a food processor or blender.
Mix in hot sauce, garlic powder, salt, pepper, and lime juice.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Chill before serving for best flavor.
